scope: Snapshot audit facts only; module-status.json remains the only current state authority.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer reproduces a Core correctness, security, missing-foundation or C++ API-usability defect.
A supported compiler or target invalidates assertion semantic parity, the one-to-eight field bound, macro hygiene, normal-path code generation, public-header closure or visibility contract.
The public API, normal-path cost, layout, compiler or environment semantics, component dependency or delivery shape changes.
A named host consumer proves that fatal-observer lifetime or coordination must be owned by Core with a different complexity or ownership shape.
A mature same-contract peer proves a better complexity class, or a normal consumer workload proves a reproducible material regression or advantage.
known_limitations: The fatal observer remains image-local and synchronously borrowed; callback exchange is not a quiescence barrier, so the embedding host owns restore and quiescence before plugin unload.
Core owns bounded typed invariant context, not arbitrary formatting, logging, backtraces, signal or minidump handling, process-wide crash policy or Native FFI.

The P0 certificate covers structural normal-path cost on the frozen candidate, toolchains and delivery shapes; it makes no failure-I/O, downstream-workload, universal timing, cache-hit, SOTA or Formal-performance claim.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer reproduces a correctness, security, ownership, lifetime, concurrency, exception-safety, API-usability or missing common intrusive-capability defect.
The public API, layout, algorithm, complexity, Core-only factor dependency, selected-header ownership or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
A supported compiler or ABI changes pointer-to-member recovery, hook layout, assumption or exception and no-exception code generation.
Time, Sched, Mem, IO or a future inference consumer proves that the current type boundary or a retained specialized link no longer matches its real contract.
A mature same-contract peer proves a better complexity class, or a normal consumer or profile proves a reproducible material regression or advantage beyond the frozen 5% margin.
Renewing the engineering claim encounters a material change in consumer provenance, peer, machine, instrument, compiler or retained evidence identity.
known_limitations: The P1 claim covers only four frozen N=4096 W1-WIN consumer replays, MSVC 19.50 and locked Boost or pre-v4 Sched peers; cross-platform timing, all operations or scales, end-to-end inference KPIs, universal SOTA and Formal are not claimed.

All intrusive containers are caller-owned stable-address thread-compatible primitives; external owners synchronize mutation, traversal, reclamation and lifetime, while wrong-owner iterators, ranges or verified counts are program-contract violations.
Safe and forward hooks require explicit retirement; forward membership has no arbitrary-node O(1) unlink, hlist is not a sorted or counted sequence, and ordinary counted range splice is O(k).

Concurrent publication or reclamation, intrusive tree, hash or heap and advanced base, value or fancy-pointer policies remain with a concurrency owner, mature peer or a future admitted consumer demand.
Sched cancellation uses the safe hlist, but waiter, pool and IOCP links retain specialized storage-reuse, publication or kernel-state contracts.
Pointer-to-member header templates expose neither Native FFI nor a stable cross-toolchain C++ ABI; retained performance artifacts are local engineering evidence and Formal remains PENDING.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer reproduces a Util-core correctness, exception-safety, ownership, lifetime, concurrency, missing-foundation or natural C++ API-usability defect.
The public API, layout, algorithm, complexity, Core-only dependency, selected-header ownership or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
A supported compiler or target invalidates conditional-noexcept, move-or-copy transfer, member-function deduction, two-word FunctionRef, no-exceptions or public-header code generation.
A frozen downstream owner proves an existing helper is being used with the wrong semantic contract, or a complete same-contract duplicate should be replaced through an explicit dependency edge.
A mature same-contract peer proves a better complexity class, or a normal consumer workload proves a reproducible material regression or advantage beyond the frozen 5% margin.
Renewing the engineering claim encounters a material change in consumer provenance, peer, machine, instrument, compiler or retained evidence identity.
known_limitations: FunctionRef remains a synchronous non-owning call-only view; storage, return and asynchronous use require an owning callable or an owner-defined function-plus-context shape.

If a resource is only potentially-throwing copyable and its deleter is move-only, failed owner move cleans the token through the transferred deleter and disarms the source; it prevents leak and double release but does not preserve source ownership after the exception.
UniqueResource is a narrow fallback for value-like native tokens, not a replacement for typed Platform, Mem or IO owners and not a general error channel.

The P1 claim covers three frozen W1-WIN FunctionRef consumer workloads against locked Abseil; cross-platform timing, all utilities or signatures, end-to-end inference, universal SOTA and Formal are not claimed.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer reproduces an Error correctness, security, ownership or lifetime, OOM or no-throw, API-usability or missing-capability defect.
A supported compiler, standard library or OS changes std::expected representation, reference lifetime diagnostics, standard-category image identity, formatting or native-translator semantics.
The public API, Status or Result layout or normal cost, direct dependency, component closure, selected-header inventory or delivery shape changes.
Renewing the engineering claim encounters a material change in frozen consumer provenance or ownership, peer, machine, instrument, compiler or retained evidence identity.
A mature same-contract peer proves a better complexity class, or a normal consumer or profile proves a reproducible material regression or advantage beyond the frozen 5% margin.
known_limitations: The P1 certificate covers only the frozen five W1-WIN consumer workloads, Abseil identity and MSVC 19.50 source/static benchmark delivery; cross-platform performance, all Error operations, end-to-end inference KPIs, universal SOTA and Formal are not claimed.

Result<T&> is a caller-owned non-null deep-const borrow and does not extend referent lifetime; nullable, range/text and shared-ownership tasks use their dedicated pointer, view/span or owning-handle shapes.
format_status retains at most 1023 bytes with an explicit truncation marker; in exception-disabled builds a custom formatter must itself obey the non-throw contract.
Custom std::error_category pointers are not retained; the category owner supplies canonical semantics and keeps its defining image alive through the adapter call.

HYLE promises neither stable C++ ABI nor Native FFI; matched headers and binaries are required, IO adoption remains IO-owned, the retained engineering bundle is local evidence and Formal remains PENDING.

reopen_triggers: A named inference or general C++ consumer proves that a model-independent numeric metric primitive, ownership contract or natural aggregation journey belonging in Obs cannot be expressed without an adapter-local reimplementation.
A reproducible correctness, concurrency, lifetime, numeric, security or C++ usability defect is demonstrated in the frozen metric, log or trace surface.
The public API, algorithm, complexity, resource contract, dependency graph, selected-header inventory or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
Qualified same-contract evidence proves a reproducible material regression, or a mature peer demonstrates a better complexity class without weakening the admitted semantics.
known_limitations: FixedHistogram boundary count is a compile-time constant while boundary values are supplied at construction; dynamic bucket schemas remain an exporter or application concern.
Concurrent metric types require an always-lock-free atomic representation, expose weakly consistent running snapshots and require quiescence for exact reset or destruction.

Counts and integral values must remain representable for the metric lifetime, floating sums follow IEEE arithmetic, and this factor provides no hidden sharding, labels, registry, exporter, time window or quantile sketch.
The engineering timing claim covers the frozen W1-WIN scheduler aggregate and a 5 percent margin; cross-platform timing and Formal certification remain pending.

reopen_triggers: A named consumer reproduces an incorrect result, undefined behavior, missing common scalar integer policy or natural C++ API-usability defect.
A supported compiler, standard library or target changes integer, GCD, bit-primitive, constexpr or normal-path code-generation semantics.
The public API, algorithm or complexity, component dependency, header closure or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
A locked llama.cpp or ggml journey, or two mature independent peers, prove a new model-independent scalar control-plane MUST.
A real batch or lane consumer admits a SIMD variant, a same-contract mechanism proves a better complexity class, or a real consumer or profile proves a reproducible material regression.
known_limitations: Math covers fixed-width non-Boolean scalar integral control-plane values; ordinary multi-operand operations use one explicit type and conversion is the only heterogeneous entry.
try_lcm is logarithmic scalar work and try_bit_ceil may use a bounded standard-library ISA selector; lane or buffer variants remain with SIMD after a real batch consumer is admitted.
Trusted scalar GCD, LCM and bit operations continue to use the C++ standard library directly; tensor, model, floating, arbitrary-precision and domain layout policy remain with their semantic owners.

The P0 claim covers complexity and structural cost on the frozen compilers and delivery shapes; nanosecond timing, every platform, end-to-end inference, universal SOTA, Native FFI and stable cross-toolchain C++ ABI are not claimed.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer exposes a correctness, security, API-usability or missing common system-time interoperability defect.
A supported platform invalidates canonical range, negative-epoch, rounding, native-field, header-isolation or output-unchanged semantics.
The public API, layout, normal cost, direct dependency, component ownership or source/static/shared delivery shape changes materially.
A profile proves a material hot-path regression, or a mature same-contract peer proves a better complexity class or reproducible material consumer advantage.
A currently routed civil, device-clock, scheduling or Native FFI journey is formally admitted with a common Time-owned value contract.
known_limitations: POSIX and Win32 native structs are C++ interoperability mechanisms, not stable wire, C FFI or cross-toolchain ABI types; Windows callers include the relevant OS header before constructing those structs.

timeval and signed Unix units lose sub-unit precision by their documented floor, truncation or timeout-ceiling route, and checked conversion can fail when a platform-defined seconds field cannot represent the value.
Calendar, timezone, text protocols, filesystem and device clocks, scheduler execution and Native FFI remain routed to their named owners rather than folded into Time interoperability.

The P0 certificate proves fixed O(1), zero unexpected resources and frozen-toolchain code shape; it does not claim universal timing SOTA, host-clock P1 renewal, end-to-end inference impact or Formal performance.

reopen_triggers: A real consumer exposes a correctness, security, owner/lifetime, ordering, concurrency, API-usability, delivery or missing-capability defect within caller-owned timer queues.
TimerEntry or queue public API/layout, radix/common algorithm, complexity or normal metadata, direct dependency, factor ownership or hyle::time facade delivery changes materially.
Sched or IO admits callback execution, wait, periodic, cross-thread command or cancellation-budget semantics that cannot remain in its owning runtime state machine.
Renewing the engineering claim encounters a material candidate, Seastar peer, Scheduler provenance/ownership, workload/accounting, machine, instrument, compiler or retained evidence change.
A mature same-contract peer proves a better complexity class, or a normal consumer/profile proves a reproducible regression beyond the frozen 5% margin.
known_limitations: The P1 WIN covers only W1-WIN and the frozen N=64 Scheduler timer lifecycle against the pinned Seastar timer_set; other cardinalities, every timer operation, cross-platform performance, end-to-end inference KPIs, universal SOTA and Formal are not claimed.

TimerEntry and both queues are caller-owned single-owner structures: linked addresses must remain stable, queues do not execute callbacks or wake waiters, and the consumer must drain detached delivery lists before rearm or destruction.
Cancelling the current radix minimum may preserve one conservative early wake to keep cancel O(1), and delivery across radix buckets is not promised to be globally ordered.
CommonTimeoutQueue has correctness and O(1) arm/cancel/next plus output-sensitive advance evidence but no current HYLE product performance consumer, so no P1 ranking is claimed for it.
The internal factor is header-only and does not create a binary or Native FFI/C API; ordinary users consume it through the hyle::time C++ product facade, with no stable C++ ABI promise.

reopen_triggers: A named consumer reproduces a Platform node-memory, CPU or host-fact correctness, security, ownership, concurrency, error or natural C++ API-usability defect.
The public API, OS semantics, algorithm, complexity, dependency graph or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
A named inference journey proves that deferred node distance, bandwidth, residency or pressure capability belongs in Platform.
Qualified same-contract or consumer evidence proves a reproducible material regression or a mature peer proves a better complexity class.
known_limitations: Multi-node Windows exposes current free and zeroed bytes but no trustworthy per-node total, so physical_total_bytes is absent there.
Linux per-node available memory is a planning estimate without the global MemAvailable watermark correction; snapshots are not reservations or allocation-success promises.
Process-wide cgroup, job and commit constraints stay in host_memory_info and must be composed once by the consumer rather than copied onto every node.
This round has native Windows, Linux and macOS coverage but no Windows multi-node hardware coverage; its P1 claim is only the W1-WIN host-planning snapshot at a 5% margin.

reopen_triggers: The selected Rust upstream revision, source bytes, license option or HYLE adapted parker state machine changes.
A named consumer reproduces a wait/thread correctness, lifetime, progress, cancellation or C++ API-usability defect.
The public API, wait algorithm, memory-order contract, layout, component dependency or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
A same-contract mechanism proves a better complexity class, or a qualified normal consumer workload proves a reproducible material regression.
known_limitations: This round signs the Rust-derived parker provenance, license and unchanged P0 cost structure; it does not rebind historical timing points into a new cross-platform P1 claim.
Thread priority and affinity controls remain subject to OS permissions and can fail through Status; they are mechanisms rather than scheduler policy.
The C++ API does not promise a stable cross-toolchain ABI, a C API or Native FFI.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer reproduces synchronous file correctness, ownership, EOF, short-transfer, EINTR, close or C++ usability failure.
The public API, complexity, native-call cost or semantics, direct dependencies, delivery, or measured product bytes change materially.
Qualified same-contract normal-consumer evidence proves a reproducible regression beyond the 5% material margin, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class.
A supported OS or SDK changes the file-handle or synchronous-I/O contract used by this factor.
known_limitations: This factor owns synchronous buffered file-handle and namespace journeys; asynchronous and direct I/O remain with the IO owner.
POSIX EINTR retry is limited to restart-safe controls without known side effects; close-like or potentially committed operations are intentionally not retried blindly.
The numeric receipt covers one warmed 4 MiB model-file journey on W1-WIN; cold-cache, other filesystems, cross-machine ranking and Formal SOTA remain unclaimed.
W1-WSL and M1-MAC provide correctness, sanitizer and delivery coverage and are not pooled with Windows NTFS timing.

reopen_triggers: A named real consumer reproduces reader, retire, lifetime, callback, ownership or C++ API-usability failure.
A supported compiler, atomic-wait or TLS implementation invalidates the epoch, route or teardown contract.
The public API or layout, algorithm, direct dependency, normal cost or source/static/shared delivery changes materially.
A qualified same-contract peer or normal consumer profile proves a material regression or promotes the path to P2.
A real consumer formally admits stalled-reader-independent hazard, GPU-fence or executor-affine reclamation that has no natural existing owner.
known_limitations: Domain, payload and intrusive record are caller-owned; the domain outlives guards and pending records, guards exit on their entry thread, and drain or destruction requires external quiescence.
A stalled reader delays its whole domain; callbacks run synchronously on the collector thread, and the 65th concurrent live thread onward shares bounded fallback stripes.
The P1 claim covers one W1-WIN short immutable-read contract; writer-side, long-reader, fallback-contention, end-to-end token-latency, cross-platform ranking and Formal performance remain unclaimed.

reopen_triggers: A real consumer reproduces an allocator/resource/buffer/pool/arena/planner correctness, OOM, lifetime, concurrency, ownership or C++ usability defect, or proves a routed family cannot perform a named foundation task.
The locked mimalloc or a direct HYLE dependency changes source, semantics, default policy, ABI, code generation or delivery on the product path.
The public API, layout, default metadata, complexity, component dependency, delivery shape or system-fact semantics changes.
A same-contract normal consumer workload proves a material regression, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class.
New OS, NUMA or large-page facts invalidate the current unknown, partial-outcome or placement contract.
known_limitations: A growable variable-size individual-free pool is routed through standard PMR over a HYLE resource rather than duplicated as a distinct HYLE owner.
Large-page arena partial effects are observable but not rollbackable; physical page granularity and NUMA placement remain unverified when the vendor or OS cannot prove them.
Tensor/KV eviction, asynchronous completion, device providers, IPC protocols and secure-secret policy remain upper-layer owners.
The P1 receipt covers one W1-WIN isolated runtime-erased heap lifecycle; other families are structural and this is not an all-platform, all-shape or Formal SOTA certificate.

reopen_triggers: A real loader, scheduler or IPC consumer reproduces a mapping, hole, access, flush, lock, shared-publication, guarded-stack, placement, lifetime or C++ usability defect.
A supported OS adds a safe same-contract partial-unmap or file-discard primitive, or changes an adopted mapping syscall contract.
The public API, layout, normal metadata/allocation/syscall cost, Platform/Error/Mem dependency, component graph or delivery shape changes.
A same-contract normal model-loader workload proves a material regression, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class.
Async/direct IO, persistent memory or device mapping gains a named foundation consumer that cannot compose the current owner routes.
known_limitations: Windows whole-view mappings have no safe partial-unmap equivalent, and file-backed kDontNeed is rejected instead of using a content-weakening anonymous-memory primitive.
SharedMapping payload size, readiness and synchronization are an external IPC protocol; Darwin and Windows native capacities may be page-rounded.
Existing borrowed pointers, spans and views must not outlive owner release, reset or move; checked accessors prevent new cross-hole views but do not track prior borrows.
The Linux model-loader P1 receipt is from W1-WSL guest engineering and is not a native-Linux, independent-hardware or Formal certificate.

reopen_triggers: A named inference or foundation consumer proves a missing model-independent row primitive that the expert seam cannot naturally carry.
A real consumer profile proves the top-k 4–8 ns diagnostic or another route has material end-to-end impact, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class.
An adopted Highway, xsimd or VQSort update changes semantics, code generation, licensing or delivery for a used primitive.
The public API or layout, target/provider route, normal dispatch/allocation/state cost, Core/Platform dependency, component graph, or source/static/shared expert delivery changes.
A supported ISA, compiler or OS cannot preserve correctness, baseline SIGILL safety, fixed/exact zero-selector cost, or fat whole-buffer single-selector cost.
known_limitations: P1 covers three inference rows on W1-WIN MSVC exact AVX2; SVE and RVV have no physical performance receipt, and Formal remains PENDING.

The same-contract n=256/k=6 top-k row is consistently about 0.95%–1.58% behind its bounded peer; code size and branch routing provide a mechanism, but no real-engine profile provides a material consumer key.
Block quantization, GEMM, attention, RoPE, Mamba, tensor fusion and sampling policy remain owned by Compute, format or engine layers rather than ordinary SIMD.

Unknown-CPU ordinary fat calls may pay one cached indirect call per whole buffer; zero selector cost is promised only for fixed or exact targets, and no Native FFI or cross-toolchain stable C++ ABI is provided.

reopen_triggers: A named consumer reproduces a sequential container correctness, security, OOM, lifetime, invalidation or natural C++ API-usability defect, or proves a missing common Container-owned capability.
A public API or layout, normal algorithm or metadata cost, allocator, hash, ISA/provider route, dependency graph or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
An adopted Highway, xxHash or wyhash update changes semantics, code generation, licensing or delivery on a used Container path.
Qualified same-contract or real-consumer evidence proves a material regression, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class for an admitted workload.
known_limitations: The P1 claim covers one frozen 4096-entry entry-and-weight LRU model-cache workload on W1-WIN; it is not an all-container, cross-platform or Formal SOTA certificate.
Standard containers remain the route where HYLE cannot supply a distinct layout, complexity, ownership or failure contract; Container does not promise full std, Boost or Folly API parity.
Tokenizer automata, KV or device cache policy, blocking service, compressed rank/select structures and model-specific storage remain higher-layer owners.
The product is C++23 source, static and shared delivery for compatible C++ toolchains without a Native FFI, C API or stable cross-toolchain C++ ABI.

reopen_triggers: A named consumer reproduces a concurrent map, set or vector correctness, security, publication, reclamation, lifetime, OOM or natural C++ API-usability defect, or proves a missing common concurrent-container capability.
A public API or layout, shard, table, reclamation or progress algorithm, allocator policy, dependency graph or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
The mem_reclaim contract used by the reclaiming node-map route changes in a way that affects lifetime, synchronization or cost.
Qualified same-contract or real-consumer evidence proves a material regression, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class for an admitted concurrent workload.
known_limitations: The P1 claim covers one frozen eight-worker read-mostly membership workload on W1-WIN; exact superiority is inconclusive and no all-operation, cross-platform or Formal SOTA claim is made.
Custom Alloc, Hash and Eq policies can be called concurrently by different shards and must themselves satisfy the documented concurrency contract.
Node address stability is limited to the documented guard lifetime; destruction requires external quiescence, and the default node map trades retained old tables for a zero read-side reclamation tax.
The factor is a private build and dependency boundary behind the C++ Container product, not a Native FFI, C API or stable cross-toolchain C++ ABI.

reopen_triggers: A named consumer reproduces a queue correctness, security, progress, FIFO, OOM, lifetime or natural C++ API-usability defect, or proves a missing common handoff or work-sharing capability.
A public API or layout, queue or progress algorithm, allocator policy, dependency graph or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
A real Scheduler or IO consumer proves that an excluded storage-level semantic cannot be composed above the current try-only queue contract.
Qualified same-contract or real-consumer evidence proves a material regression, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class for an admitted queue workload.
known_limitations: The P1 claim covers one frozen unbounded typed 4P4C handoff workload on W1-WIN; it is not an all-queue, cross-platform or Formal SOTA certificate.
UnboundedQueue payload construction, extraction callback and destruction require the documented nothrow behavior; its allocator may see producer allocation and consumer deallocation concurrently.
Queue destruction requires quiescence, and try-only storage deliberately does not own waiting, close, cancellation, deadline or backpressure service policy.
The factor is a private build and dependency boundary behind the C++ Container product, not a Native FFI, C API or stable cross-toolchain C++ ABI.

reopen_triggers: A named consumer reproduces a borrowed-text, path, interner or Unicode correctness, security, lifetime, OOM or natural C++ API-usability defect, or proves a missing common Container-owned text capability.
A public API or layout, Unicode error or complete-write semantic, provider or ISA route, allocator, dependency graph or source, static or shared delivery shape changes.
An adopted simdutf or Highway update changes semantics, code generation, licensing or delivery on a used Container Text path.
Qualified same-contract or real-consumer evidence proves a material regression, or a mature peer proves a better complexity class for an admitted text workload.
known_limitations: The P1 claim covers one frozen safe UTF-8-to-UTF-16 caller-buffer workload on W1-WIN; it is not an all-text, cross-platform or Formal SOTA certificate.
StringView and lookup results are borrowed; UTF input and output are caller-owned, undeclared overlap is unsupported, and output-too-small performs no partial conversion.
Container Text deliberately does not own locale, normalization, grapheme segmentation, regex, tokenizer automata, filesystem IO or a general owning-string policy.
simdutf is a private implementation provider, and the factor is a private build boundary behind the C++ Container product without a Native FFI, C API or stable cross-toolchain C++ ABI.

material_contribution.derivation: inference runtimes retain active backend, worker, request and block membership; a payload-free read-mostly set is the natural primitive

ownership_topology.candidate: The container_concurrent factor owns one pre-reserved HYLE ConcurrentFlatHashSet with 32768 integral keys using StableHash, std::equal_to and SystemAllocator, then serves eight pinned read-only workers
ownership_topology.equivalence: Construction, recoverable reserve/population and warmup are excluded; both charge exactly 33554432 50-percent-hit contains operations with identical hash/equality/allocation policy, no dummy mapped payload and no external locks
ownership_topology.peer: One pre-reserved oneTBB concurrent_unordered_set owns the identical keys using StableHash, std::equal_to and SystemStdAllocator over the same backend, then serves the identical pinned workers

contract_workload.semantic_contract: Answer 33554432 deterministic 50-percent-hit membership queries from eight persistent physical-core workers against one immutable 32768-entry set
contract_workload.setup: Both sets are reserved, populated and warmed before timing; workers are created and pinned before the common start barrier

audit.same_contract_audit: Frozen workload is strictly immutable: same 32768 entries, StableHash/equality/system allocator, prebuilt warmed owners and eight pinned workers, 33554432 50%-hit queries. Setup/thread creation/population excluded; complete wall-throughput interval and checksum charged.
audit.order_placement_resolution: Both medians negative (1.18/2.23% throughput), both CIs cross 1; only execution reversal, no product placement stratum. No causal timing conclusion.
audit.mechanism: HYLE contains enters/releases a shard shared lock (reader admission/removal RMW); this protects concurrent erase. oneTBB warmed find traverses atomic links and offers unsafe_erase only. This explains different cost obligations, not their measured difference or removable HYLE overhead.
audit.consumer_value: Generic active-object registry provenance, not a captured hot trace; no production HYLE set call site establishes immutable-only lifetime or 50% misses.
audit.action: Immutable task comparison remains valid. Extrapolation to equal concurrent-erasure guarantees is NOT_COMPARABLE; do not remove synchronization or weaken API to chase this row.

ownership_topology.candidate: The container_queue factor owns every in-flight uint64_t in one HYLE UnboundedQueue between four pinned producers and four pinned consumers using SystemAllocator; enqueue returns recoverable allocation failure

contract_workload.semantic_contract: Transfer 1048576 typed values exactly once through one unbounded FIFO-compatible MPMC queue using four producers and four consumers, charging 2097152 push/pop operations
contract_workload.setup: Queue construction and one complete 32768-item-per-role warmup are outside timing; workers are created and pinned before the common start barrier

audit.reason: All CURRENT strata are WIN with positive medians; outside the weak-cell screen. No expansion into unmeasured operations.

input.distribution: 256 deterministic valid 128-byte metadata records containing ASCII and two three-byte scalar sequences

material_contribution.denominator: 256 independent 128-byte metadata records represented as 4096 eight-byte measurement units
material_contribution.derivation: ggml and llama.cpp perform native UTF-16 boundary conversion while every reviewed engine carries model and token metadata through native boundaries

ownership_topology.candidate: The container_text factor validates, computes exact required UTF-16 units and converts 256 caller-owned records into caller-owned pre-sized output through the public typed result
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both charge the complete safe no-allocation three-pass contract and reject malformed or undersized output before writing; the validator compares status, input offset, required/output count and untouched output
ownership_topology.peer: The product-locked simdutf implementation pointer performs validate-with-errors, exact UTF-16 length and endian-correct valid-input conversion, then returns the identical UtfResult fields

pair.candidate: HYLE UTF-8 to UTF-16 units N=4096
pair.peer: simdutf UtfResult-adapted UTF-8 to UTF-16 units N=4096

contract_workload.semantic_contract: Validate, size and convert 32768 bytes of mixed ASCII and multibyte UTF-8 in 256 independent records to exact caller-owned UTF-16 output
contract_workload.setup: Inputs and exact-sized outputs are allocated and initialized outside measurement in controlled owner order

audit.same_contract_audit: Same simdutf pointer, validate-with-errors, exact sizing, endian-correct valid conversion, status/offset/count, untouched output on failure; caller buffers allocated outside timing, one worker.
audit.order_placement_resolution: 5/8 negative; order/allocation/placement reversals. Seven CIs cross 1, the eighth is above 1. Old all-negative text candidate excluded.
audit.mechanism: Both pay three required scans; wrappers differ in check order but no extra scan/allocation or proven causal cost.
audit.consumer_value: Model/native path boundary exists; 256 x 128-byte records (32768 bytes, 4096 eight-byte measurement units) is not 4096 records or production frequency.
audit.action: No product FIX; weakening validation/output contract is disallowed.
